summary: Include the full Biome-suppressed node in the approval identity
body: Biome’s `biome-ignore` suppresses the next syntax node, but this identity hashes only its next physical line. If an approved directive precedes a multiline node, changing code later within that node leaves the ID unchanged, so the landing check accepts the old approval for changed, still-suppressed code. Include the full covered node in the identity or invalidate approval when any covered code changes.

summary: Match block enables to the rules they re-enable
body: An `eslint-disable` for rules `a, b` followed by `eslint-enable a` leaves rule `b` disabled, but this stack pops the whole block at that enable. The identity then excludes code after the enable; adding code still suppressed by `b` leaves the approved ID unchanged and the check can report clear. Track which rules remain disabled before ending the block’s covered scope.

summary: Check legacy landing runs for switch-offs
body: This check is added to contract-2 Stage F, but runs without `coachman_contract` 2 follow Legacy Stage F, which still grants or withholds without running `landing switch-offs` or asking for approval. Such a run can therefore land a newly added suppression without the user’s word, contrary to the stated behavior for runs dispatched before this check existed. Add the check to the legacy landing path as well.

summary: Validate the card’s switch-off section against the final branch
body: The coachman is told to paste this section, but landing does not verify it: the existing card check validates only the `card-block`, and no new check compares `## Switch-offs` with the current command output. A card that omits or has a stale list can still pass landing, so the ship card may not show the final branch’s entries as required. Add and run a deterministic card-section check; this also follows [AGENTS.md:219-220].
